questions.q: What does one line of a payment term produce on an invoice?
options: One supplier site
One installment, with its own due date
One purchase order
One tax code
questions.explain: Each payment term line produces one installment, which can carry a percentage or fixed amount and its own due date.

questions.q: A payment term uses the 'Days' method with a value of 30, and an invoice is dated March 1. What is the due date?
options: March 30
April 1
The 30th of whatever month the term's fixed date specifies
March 31
questions.explain: Days adds the specified number of days to the terms date: March 1 + 30 days = March 31.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the 'Fixed Date' due date type?
options: It makes the installment due on a specific day, month, and year, regardless of the invoice date
It adds a set number of days to the invoice date
It automatically applies a discount
It is only used for prepayments
questions.explain: Fixed Date terms are due on a specific calendar date no matter when the invoice itself was dated, useful for things like an annual contract.

questions.q: In a '2/10, Net 30' payment term, what does the '2/10' part mean?
options: A 2% late fee applies after 10 days
A 10% discount applies within 2 days
A 2% discount applies if the invoice is paid within 10 days of the terms date
The invoice must be matched within 2 days of receiving it
questions.explain: The discount tier offers a 2% discount if payment happens within 10 days; otherwise the full Net 30 amount is due.

questions.q: What is the role of a 'cutoff day' on a payment term?
options: It determines the day of the month after which the due date rolls forward to a later month
It cancels the invoice if not paid by that day
It sets the supplier's bank account cutoff for wire transfers
It is the last day an invoice can be entered
questions.explain: A cutoff day controls whether the due date calculation advances to a future month, used for terms like 'due the 15th of next month.'
